reason: The hypothesis directly restates the findings of P23 and P30, which already studied Q235 steel passivation at 20, 40, and 60 °C in simulated concrete pore solution, reported faster passivation and more Fe2O3 at higher temperatures, and used the same electrochemical and surface analysis methods. The only change is a slight shift in environment (chloride-containing vs. concrete pore solution) without justification, making it a minor variation of an existing result.
copied_elements: higher temperature accelerates passive film formation
more Fe2O3 produced at higher temperature
thicker, better passive film at higher temperature
